Quantifying the therapeutic alliance: A methodological framework for conducting observational moment-by-moment research

This is a step-by-step guide to illustrate the contents of the paper “Quantifying the therapeutic alliance: A methodological framework for conducting observational moment-by-moment research”.

1. Preprocessing (observational data)

1.1 Load the observational data and merge the different files

Sometimes, data from different observations are stored in separate files. To prepare the data, we will merge them into a single file. The Observer XT provides .xlsx data files that contain several variables. For the data analysis, only a few of them are relevant:

  • Behavior: Contains the names of the coded events in a longitudinal format.
  • Observation: Contains the name assigned to each observation session. When coding, researchers must ensure that each session has a unique name. A common practice is to include an ID for the case and the session number (e.g., case1_session1). This variable represents repeated measures in a long format, as it includes all coded events within a session.
  • Subject: Identifies the individual who emits the behavior (e.g., “Therapist” or “Client”).

The researcher may choose to retain the remaining variables. However, for simplicity, we will remove them since they are not needed for our analyses. If the researcher chooses to retain the additional variables and the data frames contain different variables (as in our case), the merge function should be used. 

library(readxl)

# Load the data files

data_1 <- read_excel("data_1.xlsx")[, c("Observation", "Subject", "Behavior")]
data_2 <- read_excel("data_2.xlsx")[, c("Observation", "Subject", "Behavior")]
data_3 <- read_excel("dyad 31.xlsx")[, c("Observation", "Subject", "Behavior")]
data_4 <- read_excel("dyad 32.xlsx")[, c("Observation", "Subject", "Behavior")]



# Merge the data (only three variables)

data <- rbind(data_1, data_2, data_3, data_4)


library(writexl)
write_xlsx(data, "Previous data.xlsx")

# Maintain the remaining variables

data <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("Observation", "Subject", "Behavior"), all = T),
                      list(data_1, data_2, data_3, data_4))

1.3 Permanent grouping of behaviors

Some behaviors, either for theoretical reasons or due to their low frequency, need to be grouped. In future sections, we will present a more flexible approach for grouping behaviors for specific analyses without the need to permanently modify the dataset. However, some researchers may prefer to group behaviors permanently beforehand if they are certain that these behaviors should remain unified under the same label. In such cases, researchers may find the permanent_group function useful.

  • permanent_group allows researchers to group behaviors under a single label before conducting analyses. Its simple usage requires researchers to input the names of the behaviors to be grouped, separated by a + symbol, as well as the name of the variable that store the behaviors and the name of the new grouped behavior created.
library(readxl)
data <- read_excel("Preprocessed data - phase names.xlsx")

permanent_group <- function(data, behavior_column, behaviors_to_group, new_group_name) {
  # Check if the behavior column exists in the data
  if (!(behavior_column %in% colnames(data))) {
    stop(paste("Warning: The column", behavior_column, "does not exist in the dataset. Please check the column name."))
  }
  
  # Split the input behaviors by "+" and remove extra spaces
  behaviors_list <- strsplit(behaviors_to_group, " \\+ ")[[1]]
  
  # Check if any of the behaviors in the list are already grouped
  grouped_behaviors <- data[[behavior_column]] %in% behaviors_list
  if (any(grouped_behaviors, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    # Check if the group is already present in the column, excluding NAs
    if (any(data[[behavior_column]] == new_group_name, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      warning(paste("The behavior(s) have already been grouped under", new_group_name, "and cannot be grouped again."))
    }
  }
  
  # Update the behavior column in the dataset, ignoring NA values
  data[[behavior_column]] <- sapply(data[[behavior_column]], function(x) {
    # If the behavior contains any of the specified behaviors, replace them with the new group name
    if (is.character(x) && any(sapply(behaviors_list, function(b) grepl(b, x)))) {
      return(new_group_name)
    } else {
      return(x)
    }
  })
  
  # Return the modified dataset
  return(data)
}

As an example, the client behaviors Partial agreement and Disagreement, which are theoretically related, will be unified into the new behavior Group_1.

data <- permanent_group(data, "Behavior", "Partial agreement C + Disagreement C", "Group_1")

After preprocessing the data and obtaining the final dataset, it is always good practice to store it safely to avoid losing information and repeating the entire process.

library(writexl)
write_xlsx(data, "Preprocessed data.xlsx")

2. Descriptive statistics (observational data)

Descriptive data will be useful for future decisions regarding the analyses. To provide a comprehensive description of the data, the function sequence_descriptives is able to provide descriptive statistics for both individual behaviors and sequences of an indefinite number of behaviors. The contents of this section will, therefore, apply to both individual behaviors and sequences.

2.1 Individual behaviors and sequences: descriptive statistics, normality tests and density distribution plots

The sequence_descriptives function is designed to analyze the relative frequencies of behavior sequences across multiple phases of treatment. It provides descriptive statistics, tests for normality (Shapiro-Wilk test), and generates histograms with density distributions to visualize the distribution of behaviors/sequences. The function is highly flexible, allowing researchers to group behaviors using the + symbol without permanently altering the dataset.

Key Features

  1. Flexible Behavior Grouping:

    • Researchers can group behaviors using the + symbol (e.g., "BehaviorA + BehaviorB") to treat them as the same during analysis.
    • This grouping is applied dynamically and does not modify the original dataset.

  2. Descriptive Statistics:

    • Computes the following statistics for each treatment phase:
      • Sample size: Number of observation sessions per phase.
      • Mean: Mean relative frequency of behaviors/sequences.
      • Median: Median relative frequency of behaviors/sequences.
      • Standard deviation: Variability of relative frequencies.
      • Percentile 5: 5th percentile of relative frequencies.
      • Percentile 95: 95th percentile of relative frequencies.
      • Skewness: Measure of distribution asymmetry.
      • Standard error of skewness: Error associated with skewness.
      • Kurtosis: Measure of distribution tailedness.
    • Includes the Shapiro-Wilk test for normality, with a p-value and a variable indicating whether the distribution is Normal or Not normal.

  3. Visualizations:

    • Generates boxplots for each treatment phase.
    • Allows combining plots for all phases into a single display and group comparisons based on a variable (e.g. Intervention A vs Intervention B). Boxplots comparing groups could be displayed in the same plot or separated in different plots.

  4. Group Analysis:

    • Provides options to filter and compare specific groups or phases.

  5. Relative or Absolute Frequencies:

    • Allows absolute or relative frequencies analyses of behaviors/sequences per observation session.

  6. Requested Libraries Handling:

    • Checks for required packages (dplyr, ggplot2, gridExtra, e1071 and stats [included in the in base R]) and provides a warning if they are not installed.

Function Arguments

Argument Description
data The dataset containing the observations. It should be a data.frame where each row represents a subject’s observation within a phase of the treatment.
treatment_phase_var The name of the variable that defines the treatment phase in the dataset (e.g., "Treatment_Phase"). This variable is used to group observations by phase.
phase_order A vector specifying the order of the treatment phases to be analyzed. Example: c("Phase1", "Phase2", "Phase3"). If NULL, phases are ordered as they appear in the data.
behavior_var The name of the variable containing the observed behaviors for each subject (e.g., "Behavior"). This variable should include behavior sequences to analyze.
sequence A vector or list of strings specifying the behavior sequence to analyze. Use + to group behaviors (e.g., c("BehaviorA + BehaviorB", "BehaviorC").
combine_plots A logical value (TRUE or FALSE). If TRUE, boxes for all groups are combined into a single display. If FALSE, plots are displayed separately for each group.
group_var The name of the grouping variable used to divide the data into different groups (e.g., "Group"). If NULL, the data is analyzed as a whole.
selected_groups A vector of group names to filter and analyze. Example: c("Group1", "Group2"). If NULL, all groups in group_var are analyzed.
use_relative_frequency A logical value (TRUE or FALSE). If TRUE, relative frequencies will be computed. If FALSE, absolute frequencies will be computed.

Function syntax

sequence_descriptives <- function(data, treatment_phase_var, phase_order, behavior_var, sequence,
                                  combine_plots = FALSE, group_var = NULL,
                                  selected_groups = NULL, use_relative_frequency = TRUE) {
  
  # Required packages
  required_packages <- c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "gridExtra", "e1071", "stats")
  missing_packages <- required_packages[!required_packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]]
  if(length(missing_packages) > 0) {
    stop("The following required packages are missing: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
         "\nPlease install them using install.packages() before running the function.")
  }
  
  # Load packages quietly
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr, quietly = TRUE)
    library(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE)
    library(gridExtra, quietly = TRUE)
    library(e1071, quietly = TRUE)
    library(stats, quietly = TRUE)
  })
  
  process_behavior_group <- function(group) {
    strsplit(group, " \\+ ")[[1]]
  }
  
  # Convert phase_order to factor to maintain order
  phase_order <- factor(phase_order, levels = unique(phase_order))
  
  if (!is.null(group_var) && !is.null(selected_groups)) {
    data <- data %>% filter(.data[[group_var]] %in% selected_groups)
  }
  
  compute_sequence_frequencies <- function(treatment_phase, sequence, subset_data) {
    filtered_data <- subset_data %>%
      filter(.data[[treatment_phase_var]] == treatment_phase)
    
    sequence_data <- data.frame(
      Observation = unique(filtered_data$Observation),
      Sequence_Frequency = 0,
      Total_Possible_Sequences = 0,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    for (obs in sequence_data$Observation) {
      obs_data <- filtered_data %>% filter(Observation == obs)
      behavior_sequence <- obs_data[[behavior_var]]
      
      total_possible_sequences <- length(behavior_sequence) - length(sequence) + 1
      sequence_found <- 0
      
      if (total_possible_sequences > 0) {
        for (i in 1:total_possible_sequences) {
          window <- behavior_sequence[i:(i + length(sequence) - 1)]
          match_found <- TRUE
          
          for (j in seq_along(sequence)) {
            behavior_group <- process_behavior_group(sequence[j])
            if (!(window[j] %in% behavior_group)) {
              match_found <- FALSE
              break
            }
          }
          if (match_found) sequence_found <- sequence_found + 1
        }
      }
      
      sequence_data$Sequence_Frequency[sequence_data$Observation == obs] <- sequence_found
      sequence_data$Total_Possible_Sequences[sequence_data$Observation == obs] <- total_possible_sequences
    }
    
    if (use_relative_frequency) {
      sequence_data <- sequence_data %>%
        mutate(Frequency = ifelse(Total_Possible_Sequences > 0, Sequence_Frequency / Total_Possible_Sequences, 0))
    } else {
      sequence_data <- sequence_data %>%
        mutate(Frequency = Sequence_Frequency)
    }
    
    return(sequence_data)
  }
  
  # Prepare data frame for statistics
  all_phase_stats <- data.frame(
    Sequence = character(),
    Group = character(),
    Treatment_Phase = factor(character(), levels = levels(phase_order)),
    Sample_Size = integer(),
    Mean = numeric(),
    Median = numeric(),
    SD = numeric(),
    Percentile_5 = numeric(),
    Percentile_95 = numeric(),
    Skewness = numeric(),
    Skewness_SE = numeric(),
    Kurtosis = numeric(),
    Shapiro_p_value = numeric(),
    Normality = character(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Prepare data frame for plotting
  all_plot_data <- data.frame(
    Observation = character(),
    Frequency = numeric(),
    Treatment_Phase = factor(character(), levels = levels(phase_order)),
    Group = character(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  group_levels <- if (!is.null(group_var)) unique(data[[group_var]]) else list("All")
  
  for (group in group_levels) {
    subset_data <- if (!is.null(group_var)) data %>% filter(.data[[group_var]] == group) else data
    
    for (treatment_phase in levels(phase_order)) {
      sequence_frequencies <- compute_sequence_frequencies(treatment_phase, sequence, subset_data)
      
      if (nrow(sequence_frequencies) == 0 || all(sequence_frequencies$Frequency == 0)) {
        all_phase_stats <- rbind(all_phase_stats, data.frame(
          Sequence = paste(sequence, collapse = " -> "),
          Group = if (!is.null(group_var)) group else "All",
          Treatment_Phase = treatment_phase,
          Sample_Size = 0,
          Mean = 0,
          Median = 0,
          SD = 0,
          Percentile_5 = 0,
          Percentile_95 = 0,
          Skewness = 0,
          Skewness_SE = 0,
          Kurtosis = 0,
          Shapiro_p_value = NA,
          Normality = "No Data",
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        ))
      } else {
        sample_size <- nrow(sequence_frequencies)
        mean_val <- mean(sequence_frequencies$Frequency)
        median_val <- median(sequence_frequencies$Frequency)
        sd_val <- sd(sequence_frequencies$Frequency)
        percentile_5 <- quantile(sequence_frequencies$Frequency, 0.05)
        percentile_95 <- quantile(sequence_frequencies$Frequency, 0.95)
        skewness_val <- skewness(sequence_frequencies$Frequency)
        skewness_se <- sqrt(6 / sample_size)
        kurtosis_val <- kurtosis(sequence_frequencies$Frequency)
        
        normality_test <- tryCatch(
          shapiro.test(sequence_frequencies$Frequency),
          error = function(e) return(list(p.value = NA))
        )
        normality_result <- ifelse(is.na(normality_test$p.value) || normality_test$p.value > 0.05, "Normal", "Not Normal")
        
        all_phase_stats <- rbind(all_phase_stats, data.frame(
          Sequence = paste(sequence, collapse = " -> "),
          Group = if (!is.null(group_var)) group else "All",
          Treatment_Phase = treatment_phase,
          Sample_Size = sample_size,
          Mean = mean_val,
          Median = median_val,
          SD = sd_val,
          Percentile_5 = percentile_5,
          Percentile_95 = percentile_95,
          Skewness = skewness_val,
          Skewness_SE = skewness_se,
          Kurtosis = kurtosis_val,
          Shapiro_p_value = normality_test$p.value,
          Normality = normality_result,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        ))
        
        # Add to plot data
        temp_plot_data <- sequence_frequencies %>%
          select(Observation, Frequency) %>%
          mutate(Treatment_Phase = factor(treatment_phase, levels = levels(phase_order)),
                 Group = if (!is.null(group_var)) group else "All")
        
        all_plot_data <- rbind(all_plot_data, temp_plot_data)
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Create plots
  plot_list <- list()
  
  # Define color palette
  group_colors <- c("black", "red", "blue", "green", "purple", "orange")  # Extended palette
  
  if (!is.null(group_var)) {
    if (combine_plots) {
      # Combined plot showing all groups together
      p <- ggplot(all_plot_data, aes(x = Treatment_Phase, y = Frequency, color = Group)) +
        geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
        geom_jitter(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.8), 
                    size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
        scale_color_manual(values = group_colors[1:length(group_levels)]) +
        scale_x_discrete(limits = levels(phase_order)) +
        labs(
             x = "Treatment Phase",
             y = if (use_relative_frequency) "Relative Frequency" else "Absolute Frequency",
             color = "Group") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1),
              legend.position = "bottom")
      
      plot_list[["Combined Groups"]] <- p
    } else {
      # Separate plots for each group
      for (group in group_levels) {
        group_data <- all_plot_data %>% filter(Group == group)
        
        p <- ggplot(group_data, aes(x = Treatment_Phase, y = Frequency)) +
          geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "lightgray") +
          geom_jitter(size = 2, alpha = 0.6, width = 0.2, color = group_colors[which(group_levels == group)]) +
          scale_x_discrete(limits = levels(phase_order)) +
          labs(title = paste("Sequence Frequency - Group:", group),
               x = "Treatment Phase",
               y = if (use_relative_frequency) "Relative Frequency" else "Absolute Frequency") +
          theme_minimal() +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
        
        plot_list[[paste("Group:", group)]] <- p
      }
    }
  } else {
    # Single group plot (no groups specified)
    p <- ggplot(all_plot_data, aes(x = Treatment_Phase, y = Frequency)) +
      geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "lightgray") +
      geom_jitter(size = 2, alpha = 0.6, width = 0.2, color = "black") +
      scale_x_discrete(limits = levels(phase_order)) +
      labs(
           x = "Treatment Phase",
           y = if (use_relative_frequency) "Relative Frequency" else "Absolute Frequency") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
    
    plot_list[["All Data"]] <- p
  }
  
  # Display plots
  if (length(plot_list) > 1) {
    grid.arrange(grobs = plot_list, ncol = 1)
  } else {
    print(plot_list[[1]])
  }
  
  rownames(all_phase_stats) <- NULL
  
  return(list(statistics = all_phase_stats, plot_data = all_plot_data))
}

Output and usage example

results <- sequence_descriptives(
  data = data, 
  treatment_phase_var = "Treatment_Phase", 
  phase_order = c("Assessment", "Treatment planning", "Beginning of intervention", 
                  "Middle of intervention", "End of intervention"), 
  behavior_var = "Behavior", 
  sequence = c("Empathy", "Total agreement C"), 
  combine_plots = T,  # FALSE for separate plots per group
  group_var = "Group", 
  selected_groups = c("Good", "Poor"),
  use_relative_frequency = T
)

library(DT)

# Access the statistics dataframe from the results list
stats_df <- results$statistics

# Identify numeric columns (excluding any non-numeric columns you want to preserve)
numeric_cols <- names(stats_df)[sapply(stats_df, is.numeric)]

# Create the interactive datatable
datatable(stats_df, 
          options = list(
            pageLength = 5,
            scrollX = TRUE,  # Add horizontal scrolling if needed
            dom = 'Bfrtip'  # Layout elements
          )) %>%
  formatRound(columns = setdiff(numeric_cols, "Sample_Size"), digits = 3) %>%
  formatRound(columns = "Sample_Size", digits = 0)

3. Data analyses: answering the proposed research questions

3.1 Which behaviors/sequences occur more frequently than others?

The sequence_heatmap function is designed to analyze and visualize individual or sequences of behaviors. It generates a heatmap that displays the absolute or relative frequency of specific behaviors or sequences of behaviors across different moments (e.g., treatment phases). The function is highly customizable, allowing users to define behaviors/sequences and treatment phases, as well as specify the type of data desired (absolute or relative frequency). The researcher will also be able to flexibly group behaviors that they want to be treated as the same using a +, without permanently changing the data frame. It also allows for group comparison.

Key Features

  1. Behavior and Sequence Analysis:
    • Handles grouped behaviors flexibly (e.g., "BehaviorA + BehaviorB"), treating them as one single behavior.
  2. Customizable Inputs:
    • Users can specify the columns for behaviors, treatment phases, and sessions in the dataset.
    • Allows customization of treatment phase levels and the order of behaviors/sequences in the heatmap.
  3. Frequency Calculation:
    • Computes absolute frequencies (counts) or relative frequencies (proportions) of behaviors or sequences.
    • Calculates mean frequencies per phase by normalizing the sum of frequencies by the total number of sessions in each phase.
  4. Heatmap Visualization:
    • Generates a heatmap using ggplot2, with behaviors/sequences on the y-axis and treatment phases on the x-axis.
    • The fill color of the heatmap represents the absolute or relative frequency of behaviors/sequences.
  5. Custom Ordering:
    • Allows users to order behaviors/sequences in the heatmap either:
      • Personalized: In the same order as provided in custom_sequences.
      • By Frequency: Based on the total frequency of behaviors/sequences (highest to lowest).
  6. Group Separation:
    • Supports separation of data by groups (e.g., "Good", "Poor") if a group_var is provided.
    • Generates separate heatmaps for each group, ensuring that the analysis is tailored to each subset of the data.
  7. Requested Libraries Handling:
    • Checks for and loads required packages (dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, purrr, stringr) and installs them if they are not installed.

Function Arguments

Argument Description
data The input dataset containing behavioral data. This should be a data frame or with columns for behaviors, treatment phases, session identifiers and, optionally, groups.
behavior_col The column name in data that contains behaviors (default: "Behavior").
phase_col The column name in data that contains treatment phases (default: "Treatment_Phase"). This column should categorize observations into distinct phases.
session_col The column name in data that contains session identifiers (default: "Observation"). This column should uniquely identify each session or observation.
custom_sequences A vector of behaviors or sequences to analyze. Provide a list of behaviors and/or sequences using the c() command. Example: list(c("BehaviorA + BehaviorB", "BehaviorC"), c("BehaviorD", "BehaviorE"), c("Behavior F + Behavior G")).
phase_levels A vector specifying the order of treatment phases (default: NULL). Introduce a c() with the ordered names of the phases. Example: c("Phase1", "Phase2", "Phase3"). If NULL, phases are ordered as they appear in the data.
freq_type The type of frequency to compute: "absolute" (default) or "relative". Use "absolute" for raw counts or "relative" for proportions relative to total behaviors/sequences in each session. It computes the mean value across all sessions in each treatment phase.
custom_order The ordering of behaviors/sequences in the heatmap: "personalized" (default) or "frequency". Use "personalized" to maintain the order in which behaviors/sequences were introduced in custom_sequences. Use "frequency" to order behaviors/sequences from higher to lower total frequency across all phases.
group_var The column name in data that contains group identifiers (default: NULL). If provided, the function will generate separate heatmaps for each group. Example: "Group".
selected_groups A vector of groups to include in the analysis (default: NULL). If provided, only the specified groups will be analyzed. Example: c("Good", "Poor").

Function syntax

sequence_heatmap <- function(
    data, 
    behavior_col = "Behavior", 
    phase_col = "Treatment_Phase", 
    session_col = "Observation", 
    custom_sequences, 
    phase_levels = NULL, 
    freq_type = "absolute",
    custom_order = "personalized",
    group_var = NULL,
    selected_groups = NULL) {
  
  # Load libraries
  suppressWarnings({
    required_packages <- c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "tidyr", "purrr", "stringr")
    missing <- setdiff(required_packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
    if (length(missing) > 0) install.packages(missing)
    lapply(required_packages, library, character.only = TRUE)
  })
  
  # Helper
  process_behavior_group <- function(behavior) {
    strsplit(behavior, " \\+ ")[[1]] %>% trimws()
  }
  
  match_sequence <- function(observed, expected_seq) {
    if (length(observed) < length(expected_seq)) return(FALSE)
    for (i in seq_along(expected_seq)) {
      expected_behaviors <- process_behavior_group(expected_seq[i])
      if (!(observed[i] %in% expected_behaviors)) return(FALSE)
    }
    return(TRUE)
  }
  
  # Phase levels
  if (!is.null(phase_levels)) {
    data[[phase_col]] <- factor(data[[phase_col]], levels = phase_levels, ordered = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Filter by group
  if (!is.null(group_var) && !is.null(selected_groups)) {
    data <- data %>% filter(.data[[group_var]] %in% selected_groups)
  }
  
  # Determine group levels
  group_levels <- if (!is.null(group_var)) unique(data[[group_var]]) else list(NULL)
  
  for (group in group_levels) {
    data_group <- if (!is.null(group_var)) data %>% filter(.data[[group_var]] == group) else data
    
    # Prepare list of all sessions + phases
    data_group <- data_group %>%
      arrange(.data[[session_col]], .data[[phase_col]]) %>%
      group_by(.data[[session_col]], .data[[phase_col]]) %>%
      summarise(Behaviors = list(.data[[behavior_col]]), .groups = "drop")
    
    # Empty result holder
    results <- list()
    
    # Iterate over custom_sequences
    for (seq in custom_sequences) {
      seq_label <- paste(seq, collapse = " -> ")
      
      if (length(seq) == 1) {
        # Individual behavior
        target_behaviors <- process_behavior_group(seq)
        
        matched <- data_group %>%
          rowwise() %>%
          mutate(
            Frequency = sum(Behaviors %in% target_behaviors)
          ) %>%
          filter(Frequency > 0) %>%
          ungroup() %>%
          mutate(GroupSequence = seq_label)
        
        results[[seq_label]] <- matched
        
      } else {
        # Sequence of behaviors
        matched <- data_group %>%
          rowwise() %>%
          mutate(
            Frequency = sum(sapply(1:(length(Behaviors) - length(seq) + 1), function(i) {
              observed_slice <- Behaviors[i:(i + length(seq) - 1)]
              match_sequence(observed_slice, seq)
            }))
          ) %>%
          filter(Frequency > 0) %>%
          ungroup() %>%
          mutate(GroupSequence = seq_label)
        
        results[[seq_label]] <- matched
      }
    }
    
    all_matches <- bind_rows(results)
    
    # Add total sequences/behaviors per session for relative frequency
    if (freq_type == "relative") {
      total_counts <- data_group %>%
        rowwise() %>%
        mutate(Total = max(length(Behaviors) - 1, 1)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        select(.data[[session_col]], .data[[phase_col]], Total)
      
      all_matches <- all_matches %>%
        left_join(total_counts, by = c(session_col, phase_col)) %>%
        mutate(Frequency = Frequency / Total)
    }
    
    # Average across sessions
    summary_data <- all_matches %>%
      group_by(GroupSequence, .data[[phase_col]]) %>%
      summarise(Frequency = mean(Frequency), .groups = "drop")
    
    # Order
    if (custom_order == "personalized") {
      order_labels <- map_chr(custom_sequences, ~ paste(.x, collapse = " -> "))
      summary_data$GroupSequence <- factor(summary_data$GroupSequence, levels = rev(order_labels), ordered = TRUE)
    } else if (custom_order == "frequency") {
      summary_data <- summary_data %>% arrange(desc(Frequency))
      summary_data$GroupSequence <- factor(summary_data$GroupSequence, levels = rev(unique(summary_data$GroupSequence)), ordered = TRUE)
    }
    
    if (!is.null(phase_levels)) {
      summary_data[[phase_col]] <- factor(summary_data[[phase_col]], levels = phase_levels)
    }
    
    # Plot
    p <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = .data[[phase_col]], y = GroupSequence, fill = Frequency)) +
      geom_tile(color = "white") +
      scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "black") +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(
        title = if (!is.null(group_var)) paste("Sequences Heatmap - Group:", group) else "Sequences Heatmap",
        x = "Treatment Phase",
        y = "Sequences / Behaviors",
        fill = ifelse(freq_type == "absolute", "Absolute Frequency", "Relative Frequency")
      ) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
    
    print(p)
  }
}

Output: example usage

The function returns a heatmap or various heatmaps depending if the group argument includes a group variable. The following callings show different possible outputs.

2 groups compared - Relative frequency - Personalized order

sequence_heatmap(
  data = data, 
  behavior_col = "Behavior", 
  phase_col = "Treatment_Phase", 
  session_col = "Observation", 
  custom_sequences = list(
    c("Task with justification", "Total agreement C"),
    c("Task with justification", "Disagreement C + Partial agreement C"),
    c("Task with justification", "Partial agreement C"),
    c("Task without justification", "Total agreement C"),
    c("Feedback task", "Total agreement C"),
    c("Empathy", "Total agreement C"),
    c("Present success T", "Total agreement C")
  ),
  phase_levels = c("Assessment", "Treatment planning", "Beginning of intervention", "Middle of intervention", "End of intervention"),
  freq_type = "relative", 
  custom_order = "personalized",
  group_var = "Group",              
  selected_groups = c("Good", "Poor")
)

No group comparison - Absolute frequency - Order by total frequency

# Call the function with the phase levels
sequence_heatmap(
  data = data, 
  behavior_col = "Behavior", 
  phase_col = "Treatment_Phase", 
  session_col = "Observation", 
  custom_sequences = list(
    c("Total agreement T"),
    c("Empathy"),
    c("Partial agreement C"),
    c("Task without justification", "Total agreement C"),
    c("Partial agreement C + Disagreement C")),
  phase_levels = c("Assessment", "Treatment planning", "Beginning of intervention", "Middle of intervention", "End of intervention"),
  freq_type = "absolute",
  custom_order = "frequency",
  group_var = NULL,              
  selected_groups = c("Good", "Poor") # Only works if group_var is not NULL
)

3.2 How do behaviors/sequences evolve over time?

The sequence_trajectory function models how specific behavior sequences evolve across treatment phases using a standardized metric to allow comparison between different behaviors/sequences and different groups. It enables researchers to explore patterns of change (e.g., increasing, decreasing, stable) in the relative frequency of sequences, optional comparisons between groups. The function supports multiple polynomial shapes (linear, quadratic, cubic) to fit and visualize behavioral trends.

Key Features

  1. Trajectory Modeling:
    • Computes the relative frequency in a standardized metric of specific behaviors or behavior sequences across treatment phases.
    • Aggregates and averages frequencies to identify trends across sessions.
  2. Group-Based Analysis:
    • If a grouping variable is provided, trajectories are computed separately for each group (e.g., "Good" vs "Poor"), enabling comparative analysis.
  3. Behavior Grouping with Flexibility:
    • Supports combined behavior analysis using the + operator (e.g., "BehaviorA + BehaviorB") for evaluating equivalent/similar behaviors.
  4. Clean Visualization:
    • Plots behavioral trajectories using ggplot2 with clear phase separation and optional faceting by group.
  5. Phase Control:
    • Users can control the ordering of treatment phases.

Argument Descriptions

Argument Description
data The input data frame containing behavioral observation data.
sequence A character vector (or list of vectors) representing the target behavior and/or sequence(s) to analyze. Each sequence is matched as an exact temporal pattern.
behavior_var The column name containing behavior codes (default: "Behavior").
phase_var The column name indicating treatment phases (default: "Treatment_Phase").
phase_order Optional. A vector specifying the desired order of phases. If NULL, the function uses the factor levels in the data.
observation_var Column identifying individual observations/sessions (default: "Observation").
id_var Column identifying unique subjects or participants (default: "ID").
group_variable Optional. The column name for a grouping variable (e.g., "Group"). Required if comparing across groups.
groups_compared Optional. A vector of group labels to include in the analysis (e.g., c("Treatment", "Control")). Required if group_variable is specified.
shapes A character vector indicating the polynomial shapes to fit: "linear", "quadratic", and/or "cubic" (default includes all three).

Function syntax

sequence_trajectory <- function(
    data, 
    sequence,  # Can be a list of sequences
    behavior_var = "Behavior",
    phase_var = "Treatment_Phase", 
    phase_order = NULL,
    observation_var = "Observation",
    id_var = "ID",
    group_variable = NULL,
    groups_compared = NULL,
    shapes = c("linear", "quadratic", "cubic")) {
  
  # 1. Package handling
  required_packages <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "blme")
  suppressWarnings({
    missing_pkgs <- setdiff(required_packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
    if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) install.packages(missing_pkgs, quiet = TRUE)
    lapply(required_packages, library, character.only = TRUE, quietly = TRUE)
  })
  
  # 2. Data validation
  required_cols <- c(id_var, observation_var, phase_var, behavior_var)
  if (!all(required_cols %in% colnames(data))) {
    stop("Missing columns: ", paste(setdiff(required_cols, colnames(data)), collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # Convert sequence to list if not already
  if (!is.list(sequence)) sequence <- list(sequence)
  
  if (!is.null(group_variable)) {
    if (!group_variable %in% colnames(data)) {
      stop("Group variable not found in data.")
    }
    if (is.null(groups_compared)) {
      stop("Please specify groups to compare using 'groups_compared'")
    }
    data <- data %>% filter(!!sym(group_variable) %in% groups_compared)
  }
  
  # 3. Helper functions
  process_behavior_group <- function(group) {
    strsplit(group, " \\+ ")[[1]] %>% trimws()
  }
  
  match_sequence <- function(behavior_list, seq) {
    if (length(behavior_list) < length(seq)) return(FALSE)
    for (i in seq_along(seq)) {
      expected_behaviors <- process_behavior_group(seq[i])
      observed_behavior <- behavior_list[i]
      if (!(observed_behavior %in% expected_behaviors)) return(FALSE)
    }
    return(TRUE)
  }
  
  mean_cl_normal_custom <- function(x) {
    m <- mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    s <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    n <- sum(!is.na(x))
    se <- s/sqrt(n)
    data.frame(y = m, ymin = m - 1.96*se, ymax = m + 1.96*se)
  }
  
  # 4. Analysis logic for a single sequence
  run_analysis <- function(data_sub, current_sequence, group_name = NULL) {
    data_processed <- data_sub %>%
      rename(
        Behavior = !!sym(behavior_var),
        Observation = !!sym(observation_var),
        ID = !!sym(id_var),
        Treatment_Phase = !!sym(phase_var)
      ) %>%
      group_by(ID, Observation) %>%
      summarise(
        sequence_count = sum(
          sapply(1:(n() - length(current_sequence) + 1), function(i) {
            behavior_window <- Behavior[i:(i + length(current_sequence) - 1)]  
            match_sequence(behavior_window, current_sequence)
          })
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      left_join(
        data_sub %>%
          rename(
            Observation = !!sym(observation_var),
            ID = !!sym(id_var),
            Treatment_Phase = !!sym(phase_var)
          ) %>%
          distinct(ID, Observation, Treatment_Phase),
        by = c("ID", "Observation")
      ) %>%
      group_by(ID, Treatment_Phase) %>%
      summarise(
        total_sequences = sum(sequence_count, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      group_by(ID) %>%
      mutate(
        rel_frequency = total_sequences / sum(total_sequences, na.rm = TRUE)
      ) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    if (!is.null(phase_order)) {
      data_processed <- data_processed %>%
        mutate(Treatment_Phase = factor(Treatment_Phase, levels = phase_order))
    } else {
      data_processed <- data_processed %>%
        mutate(Treatment_Phase = factor(Treatment_Phase))
    }
    
    data_processed <- data_processed %>%
      mutate(time_points = as.numeric(Treatment_Phase))
    
    # Model fitting
    fit_results <- list()
    for (shape in shapes) {
      fit_results[[shape]] <- tryCatch({
        if (shape == "linear") {
          blmer(rel_frequency ~ time_points + (1 | ID), 
                data = data_processed,
                cov.prior = wishart)
        } else if (shape == "quadratic") {
          blmer(rel_frequency ~ poly(time_points, 2) + (1 | ID), 
                data = data_processed,
                cov.prior = wishart)
        } else if (shape == "cubic") {
          blmer(rel_frequency ~ poly(time_points, 3) + (1 | ID), 
                data = data_processed,
                cov.prior = wishart)
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        warning(paste("Model fitting failed for", shape, ":", e$message))
        NULL
      })
    }
    
    fit_comparison <- map_dfr(fit_results, ~ {
      if (is.null(.)) return(tibble(AIC = NA, BIC = NA))
      tibble(AIC = AIC(.), BIC = BIC(.))
    }, .id = "Model") %>%
      arrange(AIC)
    
    best_fit <- fit_comparison$Model[1]
    
    # Create plot title
    plot_title <- paste(paste(current_sequence, collapse = " -> "))
    if (!is.null(group_name)) {
      plot_title <- paste(plot_title, "-", group_name)
    }
    
    # Plot
    plot <- ggplot(data_processed, aes(x = Treatment_Phase, y = rel_frequency)) +
      geom_line(aes(group = ID), color = "gray70", alpha = 0.5) +
      geom_point(aes(group = ID), color = "gray50", size = 1, alpha = 0.3) +
      stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", color = "blue", size = 1.5) +
      stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal_custom, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.1, color = "blue") +
      ylim(0, 1) +
      labs(
        title = plot_title,
        x = phase_var,
        y = "Relative Frequency"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()+
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 15, hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = margin(5, 7, 5, 7)
      )
    # Prediction line
    if (!is.na(best_fit) && !is.null(fit_results[[best_fit]])) {
      pred_data <- data.frame(
        time_points = unique(data_processed$time_points)
      )
      
      pred_data$rel_frequency <- predict(
        fit_results[[best_fit]],
        newdata = pred_data,
        re.form = NA
      )
      
      pred_data$Treatment_Phase <- factor(
        levels(data_processed$Treatment_Phase)[pred_data$time_points],
        levels = levels(data_processed$Treatment_Phase)
      )
      
      plot <- plot +
        geom_line(
          data = pred_data,
          aes(x = Treatment_Phase, y = rel_frequency, group = 1),
          color = "red",
          size = 1.2
        ) +
        annotate(
          "text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
          label = paste("Best fit:", best_fit, "\nAIC:", round(fit_comparison$AIC[1], 1)),
          hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3
        )
    }
    
    list(
      data_processed = data_processed,
      fit_results = fit_results,
      fit_comparison = fit_comparison,
      best_fit = best_fit,
      plot = plot
    )
  }
  # 5. Main analysis logic 
  if (is.null(group_variable)) {
    results <- map(sequence, ~ run_analysis(data, .x))
    names(results) <- map_chr(sequence, ~ paste("Sequence:", paste(.x, collapse = " -> ")))
    
    return(list(
      individual_sequences = results,
      all_sequences_plot = wrap_plots(map(results, "plot"), ncol = length(sequence))
    ))
  } else {
    # With group comparison
    data_filtered <- data %>% filter(!!sym(group_variable) %in% groups_compared)
    group_list <- split(data_filtered, data_filtered[[group_variable]])
    
    # Analyze each group and sequence combination
    group_results <- map(groups_compared, function(group) {
      seq_results <- map(sequence, ~ {
        list(
          results = run_analysis(group_list[[group]], .x, group_name = group),
          label = paste("Group", group, "|", paste(.x, collapse = " -> "))
        )
      })
      names(seq_results) <- map_chr(sequence, ~ paste("Sequence:", paste(.x, collapse = " -> ")))
      
      list(
        group = group,
        sequences = seq_results,
        group_plot = wrap_plots(map(seq_results, ~ .x$results$plot), ncol = 1)
      )
    })
    names(group_results) <- paste("Group", groups_compared)
    
    # Create comparison plot
    all_plots <- map(group_results, ~ map(.x$sequences, ~ .x$results$plot)) %>% 
      flatten()
    comparison_plot <- wrap_plots(all_plots, ncol = length(groups_compared))
    
    return(list(
      by_group = group_results,
      comparison_plot = comparison_plot
    ))
  }
}

Output: example usage

The function returns a list with plots and model information:

  • For single-group analysis:
    • A list of results for each sequence.
    • A combined vertical plot (all_sequences_plot) showing the relative frequency trajectories across phases.
  • For group comparisons:
    • Results broken down by group and sequence.
    • A comparison_plot showing trajectory plots side-by-side across groups for all sequences.

Each plot includes: - Individual lines for each subject. - Group average trajectory with confidence intervals. - Best-fit polynomial model (in red) with AIC info.

Two single behaviors compared

The output shown answers the research question How do behaviors/sequences evolve over time?, so the group_variable argument is NULL.

# Two single behaviors compared

result <- sequence_trajectory(
  data = data,
  sequence = list(c("Task with justification"), c("Empathy")),
  behavior_var = "Behavior",
  phase_var = "Treatment_Phase",
  phase_order = c("Assessment", "Treatment planning", "Beginning of intervention", "Middle of intervention", "End of intervention"),
  observation_var = "Observation",
  id_var = "ID",
  group_variable = NULL,
  groups_compared = NULL,
  shapes = c("linear", "quadratic", "cubic")
)

result[["all_sequences_plot"]]

3.3 How do changes in behaviors/sequences differ across groups?

The sequence_trajectory allows for comparisons between groups using the argument group_variable, which needs to be filled with the name of the variable that contains the groups’ names. In the argument groups_compared, we need to indicate which groups from the group_variable we want to compare.

Output

One sequence - Two groups compared

result <- sequence_trajectory(
  data = data,
  sequence = list(c("Task with justification", "Total agreement C")),
  behavior_var = "Behavior",
  phase_var = "Treatment_Phase",
  phase_order = c("Assessment", "Treatment planning", "Beginning of intervention", "Middle of intervention", "End of intervention"),
  observation_var = "Observation",
  id_var = "ID",
  group_variable = "Group",
  groups_compared = c("Good", "Poor"),
  shapes = c("linear", "quadratic", "cubic")
)

result[["comparison_plot"]]

Two sequences - Two groups compared

result <- sequence_trajectory(
  data = data,
  sequence = list(c("Summarizing + Clarifying + Finishing sentence", "Total agreement C"), c("Empathy", "Total agreement C")),
  behavior_var = "Behavior",
  phase_var = "Treatment_Phase",
  phase_order = c("Assessment", "Treatment planning", "Beginning of intervention", "Middle of intervention", "End of intervention"),
  observation_var = "Observation",
  id_var = "ID",
  group_variable = "Group",
  groups_compared = c("Good", "Poor"),
  shapes = c("linear", "quadratic", "cubic")
)

result[["comparison_plot"]]
